# Emspaced

> Emspaced is a coworking space, serviced office and business-support provider in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, with locations at KL Sentral and KL Eco City. It offers hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices, meeting rooms, virtual offices, accounting services, HR management systems (HRMS) and IT solutions for freelancers, startups and SMEs.

Emspaced operates two coworking locations in Kuala Lumpur. Pricing and availability change; always confirm current plans on the Membership page or by contacting the team.

## Business facts
- Name: Emspaced
- Type: Coworking space, serviced office and business-support provider
- Country: Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur, Klang Valley)
- KL Sentral: Level 23A, Menara Allianz Sentral, 203 Jalan Tun Sambanthan, 50470 Kuala Lumpur
- KL Eco City: Level 5, Mercu 3, Jalan Bangsar, KL Eco City, 59200 Kuala Lumpur
- Phone: +60-3-7890-0205 | Mobile: +60-12-281-9553
- Website: https://jh27.life/
- Social: https://www.facebook.com/emspacedmy, https://x.com/EmspacedMY, https://www.linkedin.com/company/emspacedmy/, https://www.instagram.com/emspacedmy/

## Corpus 4: Authoritative Knowledge Base & Practical Guides
- [KL Is Becoming a Stronger Choice for Flexible Work - Here's Why That Matters for Malaysian Professionals](https://jh27.life/blog/kl-is-becoming-a-stronger-choice-for-flexible-work-heres-why-that-matters-for-malaysian-professionals/): KL has quietly become one of the more compelling cities for flexible and remote work in the region - and the numbers from the market itself tell an interesting story. According to Knight Frank Malaysia's Real Estate Highlights for the first half of 2025, office occupancy across the Klang Valley showed mixed but positive performance, with KL City reaching 69.1% occupancy and fringe areas at 89.4%. The report also highlighted continued demand for Grade A, well-located office developments, particularly those with strong connectivity. Average rents in KL City reached RM6.69 per sq ft per month in 1H 2025.
- [Choosing a Coworking Space in KL: Beyond the Desk](https://jh27.life/blog/choosing-a-coworking-space-in-kl-beyond-the-desk/): The way businesses use office space in Malaysia has changed significantly. As companies adapt to hybrid work, changing team sizes and different ways of working, flexible workspace is becoming an increasingly relevant option for businesses looking for more adaptable office solutions. Malaysia's flexible workspace sector continues to develop, with both international and local operators expanding their presence across the country. The continued introduction of new flexible workspace locations reflects growing interest in office solutions that offer businesses greater flexibility and convenience.

- [Phase 4 e-Invoicing Has Started - Here Is What Your Business Actually Needs to Do Right Now](https://jh27.life/blog/phase-4-e-invoicing-has-started-here-is-what-your-business-actually-needs-to-do-right-now/): The mandate is live. The relaxation window is open. This is what compliance looks like in practice. On 1 January 2026, Malaysia's Phase 4 e-invoicing mandate came into effect. If your business has annual revenue between RM1 million and RM5 million, you are now legally required to issue invoices through LHDN's MyInvois system - not as a PDF, not as a printed document, but as a validated digital file submitted directly to LHDN before it reaches your buyer.
- [LHDN Raised RM4.4 Billion in Additional Tax Assessments - And e-Invoicing Is Strengthening Compliance](https://jh27.life/blog/lhdn-raised-rm4-4-billion-in-additional-tax-assessments-and-e-invoicing-is-strengthening-compliance/): A figure announced at the 26th National Tax Conference in Kuala Lumpur on 4 August 2026 should be on every Malaysian business owner's radar: LHDN raised RM4.4 billion in additional tax assessments as of 30 June 2026 following its audit and compliance efforts. These are additional tax assessments arising from LHDN's audit and compliance activities. LHDN has also expanded its use of technology and artificial intelligence in tax administration, including analysing more than 1.6 billion e-Invoices to strengthen compliance and risk detection.

Most business owners think of payroll as an administrative task. It runs in the background, the numbers go out on time, and if nobody complains, the assumption is that everything is fine. The reality is more consequential than that. Payroll is one of the few business functions in Malaysia where small mistakes can create immediate legal and financial consequences. A missed submission deadline, an incorrect deduction rate, or a misclassified employee can quickly escalate into penalties, audits, or employee disputes.
